feature_candidates.description: Discretize video duration into log-scaled bins (including a zero-duration bucket) and learn per-bin embeddings concatenated to the video embedding.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Mitigates zero-duration and duration-capping confounds, likely improving ranking stability across tabs.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add a categorical feature to the video feature table using existing duration field; embed via lookup in the model's feature embedding layer.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: None; duration is a static video attribute, not derived from target or temporal aggregates.
feature_candidates.name: log_duration_bucket_embedding

feature_candidates.description: Encode the tab column as a categorical feature with dedicated embeddings, capturing position-related long_view propensity.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Leverages the sharp tab-specific long_view rate differences to improve within-user ordering.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add tab as an input feature to the group_softmax model, with an embedding matrix for the ~15 observed tab values.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Tab is a positional attribute; safe from target leakage but may overfit to tab distribution shifts if not regularized.
feature_candidates.name: tab_id_embedding

feature_candidates.description: Compute per-user, per-video historical long_view and click counts from the train split only, and use them as user-conditional item features.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Models user-specific affinity to specific videos, a signal not present in global popularity and likely to raise GAUC.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Precompute train-only user×video count matrices and feed normalized counts as additional input features to the model.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Safe if built exclusively from train interactions; must not incorporate validation/test history to avoid temporal leakage.
feature_candidates.name: user_video_affinity_history

findings.evidence: DATA CARD 'Tab Breakdown (train)' rows for tabs 0,1,4 with long_view rates 4.22%, 38.61%, 48.93%.
findings.implication: Encoding tab id as a dedicated categorical embedding should capture position-driven ranking signal and likely improve GAUC within user sessions.
findings.observation: Train tab breakdown shows long_view rates of 38.61% for tab 1, 48.93% for tab 4, but only 4.22% for tab 0, indicating large intra-user position effects.
findings.title: Tab position strongly modulates long_view

findings.evidence: DATA CARD 'Data Quality' lists 239 zero-duration videos and 24,076 affected train rows.
findings.implication: Adding per-video duration-bin embeddings (e.g., log-duration buckets) can help the model disentangle duration effects from content relevance.
findings.observation: 239 videos have zero duration, affecting 24,076 train rows, and duration capping is noted as a strong confound for long_view.
findings.title: Zero-duration videos are a confound for long_view

findings.evidence: EDA PLAN feature_hypotheses item 3 proposes user-conditional video statistics; DATA CARD confirms full user/video feature coverage.
findings.implication: Deriving user-conditional video affinity from train history (e.g., previous long_view count per video_id) may capture item-level user taste and boost GAUC.
findings.observation: Per-user historical click/long_view counts on the same video (train-only) are hypothesized to be predictive, with no existing measurement yet.
findings.title: User-conditional per-video history shows affinity potential

expected_artifacts: A train-only EDA report: per-tab long_view rate by duration bucket, and hourbin/per-day heatmaps.
A table of per-user video history counts (clicks/long_views) and their correlation with validation long_view, to guide user-conditional feature construction.
A feature correlation/importance table (e.g., mutual information or Cramer's V) for candidate features vs long_view, from train split.
A short recommendation memo specifying which features to test in the next bpr/group_softmax run, with safe feature definitions.
feature_hypotheses: Added per-video log-duration and duration-bin embedding will improve ranking because zero-duration videos (24k rows) and duration capping are strong confounds for long_view.
Encoding tab id as a categorical feature with dedicated embeddings will capture intra-user position effects (e.g., tab 1 and tab 4 show higher long_view rates).
User-conditional video statistics (e.g., user's past long_view count per video_id, derived from train history) provide leakage-safe item-level user affinity that boosts GAUC.
Time-windowed exposure frequency (number of times a user saw the same video in recent 24h) can model fatigue and recency effects for sequential ranking.
leakage_risks: The video statistics table is a full-platform period aggregate (ratio ~4892x logged exposures); any feature from it (e.g., total views) must be excluded or explicitly caveated and validated only on train.
Using user history derived from the same training period may cause temporal leakage, but since evaluation is within-user ranking and only uses train, it is safe if built from train only.

Tab id is a strong position signal; careful model design should avoid it dominating content relevance, and evaluation must ensure this does not become a shortcut that overfits to tab distribution shifts.
Duplicated rows (15,609) and zero-duration videos can distort aggregate statistics; masking or weighting these during feature construction is necessary to avoid biased estimates.
plan.objective: Plan a leakage-safe EDA pass on train+valid to identify within-user ranking signals for long_view, focusing on time, tab, duration, and per-video popularity features that can be tested by registered families (bpr, group_softmax, history_features). Avoid or caveat leaky video-statistics aggregates.
questions: How does long_view rate vary by hourbin (hour-of-day) and day-of-week within a user's session sequence?
What is the lift in long_view from tab 1 vs tab 4 and other high-CTR tabs after controlling for video duration?
Does video duration (or log-duration) show a monotonic relationship with long_view probability across tabs?
How predictive are user-conditional video popularity features (e.g., user's historical click/long_view rate on that video_id) compared to global popularity?
required_inputs: Train+valid interaction rows with existing user_id, video_id, tab, hourmin, duration, long_view, and all static user/video feature tables.
User-level and video-level aggregation scripts (train-only) to compute per-user history counts and per-video global statistics without touching test.
Registered method cards for BPR and group_softmax to confirm how new features are ingested (e.g., candidate embedding concatenation).
Existing baseline configuration (bpr_b03_seed2) as reference for reproducible feature ablation.

report.recommended_next_focus: Test duration-bin and tab embeddings in a single group_softmax experiment (e.g., gs02) while concurrently measuring user-history-affinity in bpr_b04 to isolate feature gains.
report.summary: EDA identifies tab position and video duration as the strongest leakage-safe within-user ranking signals; user-conditional per-video affinity from train history is the most promising new feature family, while global video-statistics aggregates must remain excluded.
